assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent=yes / daemon=full / driver=ready → route `record`.

### agent — yes

`hermes chat` is a long-lived interactive REPL that keeps ONE session across many
sequential turns; the scenario's compressed proxy (4 plain prompts in one session)
is the ordinary path, not an edge case. Session identity is minted once per REPL
and every turn's messages land under it (`sessions.id`, shape
`YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<hex6>`; 25 rows across the sample store, `source` in
('cli','tui')). No feature flag, slash command or mode is needed.

### daemon — full

The scenario's user-observable signals are the per-turn `ready → working → ready`
arcs, no flicker within a turn, and a final settle to `ready`. Each maps onto a
signal this adapter already produces:

- **`ready → working` at turn start.** The load-bearing question is EMISSION, not
  parsing: does the user row reach the store BEFORE the assistant reply, or does
  hermes batch the whole turn at the end? It is written first, deliberately —
  `agent/turn_context.py:1198-1207` in the hermes source carries the comment
  "Crash-resilience: persist the inbound user turn before the first LLM call" and
  calls `_ensure_db_session()` + `_persist_session(messages, ...)` before the API
  loop is entered. The watcher's next scan sees `message_count` grow with the
  newest row `role='user'`, `turnIsDone` returns false (watcher.go:426-436), and
  the fold hands the state rules `LastEventType="user_message"` → working.
- **No flicker within a turn.** `finish_reason` is an explicit turn boundary, so
  the adapter never needs an idle-flush heuristic that could settle a session
  mid-turn: `stop` → `turn_done`, `tool_calls` → `assistant_message` with open
  ToolUses (parser.go:81-95, pinned by TestParseLine_AssistantToolCallsDoesNotEndTurn
  and TestWatcher_ToolCallTurnIsNotTerminal). Mid-turn writes exist too and are
  also non-terminal: hermes flushes incrementally before tool execution
  (`agent/conversation_loop.py:5767-5772`) and after tool progress
  (`agent/tool_executor.py:138-152`), and every one of those rows is either an
  assistant/tool_calls or a tool row — neither closes the turn.
- **`working → ready` at turn end.** The assistant row with `finish_reason='stop'`
  is committed by the turn-end persist; `turnIsDone` marks the activity event
  Terminal and the fold reports `LastEventType="turn_done"`.
- **Final settle.** Same mechanism as any turn end, plus the `ended_at`
  transition emits one final terminal activity (watcher.go:408-418) when the REPL
  is torn down.

Unlike the opencode sibling on this row, there is no process-exit-before-poll race
to design around (#492): the recipe is interactive, so the `hermes chat` process
outlives every turn boundary and the terminal `stop` row is polled while the
session is still alive. The adapter is wired into the daemon at
`core/cmd/irrlichd/wiring.go:90-91` (store-watcher dispatch on adapter name) and
registered at `core/adapters/inbound/agents/all.go:33`.

### driver — ready

The recipe needs `send`, `wait_turn` and `sleep` only.
`replaydata/agents/hermes/driver-interactive.sh` declares
`DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn"` — every needed primitive is
genuinely ported, not stubbed. `wait_turn` is a real signal poll over
`messages.finish_reason='stop'` counted per session (not an idle heuristic), and
`resolve_session_id` binds only to a row whose `started_at` post-dates this
slot's launch, which is what keeps the SHARED store from handing the driver a
stale session. No `keys`/`interrupt`/`reset_session` arm is touched.

### Birth shape (why the spec looks different from the claudecode sibling)

Hermes creates its `sessions` row LAZILY, in turn setup — `_ensure_db_session()`
is called from `agent/turn_context.py:613` / `run_agent.py:607-633`, i.e. on the
first prompt, not at REPL launch. So before turn 1 the only thing the daemon can
see is its own `proc-<PID>` pre-session (the process matcher fires at launch:
`(^|/)hermes( |$)` matches the console-script argv and `chat` is not a service
subcommand). The spec therefore models the birth as two phases and pins every
post-birth phase to the store-backed id via `session_id_prefix` + `same_session_as`,
so the pre-session row — which never goes `working` — cannot steal the birth and
cascade failures.
caveats: PROVISIONAL ON TIMING (the one thing only `record` can settle): the per-turn `working` observation depends on a watcher scan landing between the user-row commit and the assistant `stop` commit. The watcher rescans on fsnotify over the store's directory plus a 2s poll backstop, with a 500ms debounce (watcher.go:19-35), so a turn that completes inside one scan gap would coalesce into a single observation and its `working` span would never be observed. Real inference turns run seconds, so this is unlikely — but it is a property of emission timing, not of the parser, and is asserted here on a code read alone.

`observations.model` is deliberately NOT pinned. The model is whatever the recording home's config.yaml sets as `model.default`; the maintainer's dev home is `gpt-5.6-luna` on provider `openai-codex` (config.yaml:1-3, and both `gpt-5.6-luna` and `google/gemma-4-26b-a4b` appear in `sessions.model` in the live store), but the isolated HERMES_HOME the rig exports has its own config. `record` should fill it from the recording.

`cost_nonzero` is deliberately NOT asserted. metrics.go:156-163 prices via irrlicht's own capacity table rather than `sessions.estimated_cost_usd` (hermes reports 0.0 with billing_mode='subscription_included'), and a grep of core/pkg/capacity/aliases.go finds no entry for `gpt-5.6-luna` or `gemma`, so EstimateCostUSD legitimately returns 0 for these models. `tokens_nonzero` is asserted instead — `sessions.input_tokens`/`output_tokens` are maintained by `update_token_counts` per API call (conversation_loop.py:2980-3010) and are non-zero in every sampled row.

`sessions.cwd` is empty for `source='cli'`, and `hermes chat` records `source='cli'`, so the project binding is borrowed from the single live hermes process (`defaultLiveCWD`, watcher.go:115-124). That probe returns "" when it finds anything other than exactly one live session process — so a second hermes running on the machine during the recording drops the binding. Recording prereq below.

Tool calls are deliberately excluded from the recipe, matching the scenario description and the committed claudecode sibling (both use 4 plain prompts). Hermes' config carries an `approvals:` block and a dangerous-command approval prompt exists in its CLI path; whether it would fire for the toolsets in play is UNVERIFIED, and the driver has no `keys`/`interrupt` primitive to answer one, so a tool-call turn could legitimately enter `waiting` and stall. Consequence: the scenario's "includes at least one tool call" bullet is NOT satisfied by this cell — same as claudecode's.

UNVERIFIED: the sample store contains PAIRS of identically-timestamped `source='cli'` rows with no `parent_session_id` (e.g. 20260802_212608_1dc71a and 20260802_212608_feed91). The cause was not established — most likely two concurrent dev runs, but a hermes-side sibling-session fork is not ruled out. Post-birth phases are pinned via `same_session_as` so a sibling row cannot break them, but `record` should check how many hermes sessions the recording surfaced.

The unbounded `no state_transition to waiting` invariant on session_birth rests on the prompts being directive one-word replies, so `ProseIndicatesWaiting` over the assistant text should not fire (parser.go:83-91). A model that answers with a clarifying question would legitimately trip it.

CONFIRMED by recording 2026-08-03-00-09-42_irrlichd-0.5.9+4aaa0b3 (2026-08-03): 9/9 spec phases pass. All FOUR per-turn arcs are separable on ONE store-backed session (20260803_000941_e4c2f1) — presession proc-30223 ready 00:09:42.081; session ready 00:09:45.756; then working/ready at 46.715/50.634, 54.716/56.428, 00:10:00.434/04.019, 07.963/12.744. Working spans 3.9s / 1.7s / 3.6s / 4.8s. No state_transition to waiting anywhere; final state ready. The store agrees exactly with the recipe's verify[]: 4 role='user' rows and 4 role='assistant' rows with finish_reason='stop' (active=1), message_count=8. This settles the PROVISIONAL ON TIMING caveat above: the per-turn working span really is emitted, because hermes commits the inbound user row before the first LLM call.

TIMING MARGIN IS THIN AND THE RECIPE'S WIDE PROMPTS ARE WHAT BUY IT. Turn 2's working span was only 1.7s against a 2s poll / 500ms debounce — i.e. slightly more than one scan gap. The one-word "Reply with exactly the word: alpha|beta|gamma|delta" prompts this cell was assessed with would very likely have collapsed at least one of the four arcs into a single observation and failed its tN_start. Do not shrink the generations on a re-record; if an arc ever does collapse, widen further rather than de-pinning the phase.

ONE session, not a pair: the UNVERIFIED caveat above worried that the sample store held PAIRS of identically-timestamped source='cli' rows. This recording surfaced exactly ONE store-backed hermes session for the run, so whatever produced those pairs is not a property of a `hermes chat` REPL run.

observations: tokens_nonzero STRIPPED, model pinned in its place (and agent=hermes added). Seen red on THIS recording before stripping: `✗ tokens: want >0 got 0`, with all 9 state phases green. The assessment note above justifying tokens_nonzero — 'sessions.input_tokens/output_tokens are maintained per API call and are non-zero in every sampled row' — is correct about the STORE and wrong about the VERIFY SURFACE: this session's sessions row really does carry input_tokens=22044 / output_tokens=403 / cache_read_tokens=53760, but of verify reads only the replay golden summary, and hermes' token vector is produced by ComputeMetrics over the store, a path the offline replay tool never runs. Same strip, same reason, as every committed hermes cell.

sources.note: reconcile() emits activity when message_count grows; turnIsDone() reads the newest active row's role+finish_reason — 'stop' on an assistant row is the terminal marker, everything else is mid-turn
role/finish_reason → event kind: user→user_message (clears open tools), assistant+stop→turn_done, assistant+tool_calls→assistant_message with ToolUses, tool→tool_result

querySessionMetrics/foldMessages: LastEventType + open-tool set come from replaying messages; token totals + cwd come from the sessions row; cost priced by irrlicht's capacity table, not sessions.estimated_cost_usd

EMISSION PROOF for the working span — 'Crash-resilience: persist the inbound user turn before the first LLM call'; _ensure_db_session() + _persist_session() run before the API loop, so the user row is committed while the turn is still in flight
_flush_session_db_after_tool_progress — incremental mid-turn flush, so tool-call/tool-result rows land during the turn (all non-terminal)
assistant tool-call turn is flushed to state.db BEFORE tool side effects run
_ensure_db_session() creates the sessions row lazily on first use (turn setup), not at REPL launch — why the store-backed session is not observable before turn 1
hermes-agent version 0.19.0 — the CLI version this assessment was read against
model.default=gpt-5.6-luna, model.provider=openai-codex on the dev home; the recording home supplies its own

DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn" — every primitive this recipe needs is ported; wait_turn polls COUNT(finish_reason='stop') per session, resolve_session_id binds only to a row started after this slot launched
hermes.New(maxSessionAge) store watcher is wired into the daemon by adapter name
recipe template for this scenario — 4 plain prompts, send/wait_turn/sleep; the tool-call variant was dropped there for the same class of reason

live store sampled read-only: session ids are YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<hex6>; SELECT source,model,MAX(input_tokens),MAX(output_tokens) GROUP BY shows non-zero token aggregates on every cli/tui row (max 54818 in / 1956 out)

preconditions: hermes >=0.19.0 on PATH (Python console script; the driver launches `hermes chat`)

HERMES_HOME exported to the recording home, with its own config.yaml carrying model.default + model.provider and working credentials — hermes writes NO transcript file, so state.db under that home is the only signal
sqlite3 on PATH (the driver reads session id and turn completion straight out of state.db)
irrlichd is recording (--attach against a daemon with --record, or isolated mode) AND the hermes 'store' observe permission is granted — a pending permission means zero monitoring
NO other hermes session process alive during the run: sessions.cwd is empty for source='cli', so the project binding is borrowed from the single live process and an ambiguous match drops it
setup: The driver launches `hermes chat` under tmux in a fresh per-run cwd under <staging>/cwd/ and polls for the 'Type your message or /help' banner before sending (the TUI takes seconds to load tools + skills; keystrokes sent early are swallowed silently)

No session id is passed: hermes mints its own YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<hex6> id, and the row is INSERTed lazily at the first prompt. resolve_session_id binds the slot to the newest cli/tui row started AFTER this slot launched, so a leftover session in the shared store cannot be adopted
No auto-mode / permission step is needed: the recipe is 4 plain prompts with no tool calls, so nothing reaches an approval gate

Every one of the four generations is deliberately WIDE (a 30-line count plus two sentences of prose) rather than the one-word "Reply with exactly the word: alpha|beta|gamma|delta" an earlier draft carried. The watcher polls every 2s with a 500ms debounce, so a ~1s turn can commit its user row and its assistant finish_reason=stop row inside a SINGLE scan — that turn's ready→working edge then never exists to be observed and its tN_start phase fails. With EIGHT such edges pinned, this cell is the one most exposed to that collapse. Widening the generation is the fix; weakening the spec is not. The four prompts stay DISTINCT (different ranges, different topics) so the turns remain individually identifiable in the store.

script.text: Without using any tools, count from 1 to 30, one number per line. Then, without using any tools, write two sentences explaining what addition is.
Without using any tools, count from 31 to 60, one number per line. Then, without using any tools, write two sentences explaining what subtraction is.
Without using any tools, count from 61 to 90, one number per line. Then, without using any tools, write two sentences explaining what multiplication is.
Without using any tools, count from 91 to 120, one number per line. Then, without using any tools, write two sentences explaining what division is.

verify: events.jsonl shows a proc-<PID> pre-session in ready shortly after `hermes chat` launches (the store row does not exist yet)

a store-backed session id of shape YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<hex6> appears and, for EACH of the 4 turns, shows exactly one ready→working transition at the prompt and exactly one working→ready transition at turn end
no state_transition to waiting fires on the store-backed session across the whole run (no tool calls, so no approval gate)
state.db contains exactly 4 rows with role='assistant' AND finish_reason='stop' for that session id, and 4 role='user' rows
the session's cum_input_tokens / cum_output_tokens are non-zero (sessions.input_tokens / output_tokens)
